summary: Twelve response-caching, ingress, download, optional-store, SAML, browser cancellation, service-worker, appcode-cache, replay-refill, and isolated-process findings are tracked to completion without introducing Redis or server-side session state.

accepted_residual_risks.disposition: A complete captured SAML exchange cannot be guaranteed globally single-use across workers without optional shared atomic state. Signed browser binding, short expiry, rate controls, and normal-browser replay rejection remain mandatory; Redis is not required.

A non-yielding trusted coroutine or blocked Python thread cannot be forcibly stopped by an in-process timeout. Optional isolated-process execution remains the killable non-streaming boundary and is not a hostile-code sandbox.

findings.disposition: Protected routes and any response carrying session state are always private/no-store; an application Cache-Control public directive cannot override the framework boundary, and intentionally public responses cannot carry Set-Cookie.
findings.compatibility_note: Authenticated or BFF responses intentionally marked public become private. Versioned public framework assets remain cacheable and do not rotate sessions.

findings.disposition: Password form, password JSON, and SAML ACS routes reject disabled features, unsupported content types, missing applications, and unknown SAML providers before body parsing; uploads then use bounded per-peer/per-worker admission plus independent idle and total deadlines.
findings.compatibility_note: Only missing-application, unsupported-content-type, stalled, over-limit, or capacity-exhausted uploads are rejected. Generous defaults are configurable and cover upload only, not authentication, SAML validation, session duration, or BFF execution.

findings.disposition: Every uncached BFF request body acquires process-local per-peer and per-worker upload admission before the first receive. Queued requests do not buffer bodies, and upload admission is released before the existing execution gate is acquired.
findings.compatibility_note: Only upload saturation is rejected. Upload capacity and queue limits are configurable and separate from backend execution timeouts, normal async concurrency, sync calls, and streaming.

findings.disposition: Appcode responses hold bounded process-local per-peer and per-worker admission until completion, disconnect, or cleanup, with independent absolute and blocked-write deadlines. Deployment-built archives are written atomically, bound to complete archive/source manifests and the framework transformer version, and can be preferred or required in production while the backend entrypoint remains installed separately.
findings.compatibility_note: Dynamic development packaging remains the default. Production can opt into immutable prebuilt archives; session-specific BFF replay clients continue using dynamic archives and cannot be combined with required prebuilt mode.

findings.disposition: Signed-cookie claims are validated locally. Every explicitly enabled shared revocation read is offloaded through bounded asynchronous admission with an operation deadline and the provider circuit breaker.
findings.compatibility_note: The remote revocation provider remains optional; normal stateless sessions require neither Redis nor another store and incur no gate or thread-pool work.

findings.disposition: Public SAML login and metadata routes apply bounded per-peer rate controls, validate the application before provider work, run toolkit and crypto work off-loop behind dedicated bounded admission, and cache metadata by a bounded effective-settings fingerprint.
findings.compatibility_note: SAML endpoint URLs, browser flow, and signed stateless handshake remain provider-compatible and require no shared state or Redis.

findings.disposition: The hosted page supplies one validated CSRF cookie name. Production JavaScript and generated BFF clients accept only __Host-pytincture-csrf; local HTTP clients accept only pytincture-dev-csrf.
findings.compatibility_note: Local HTTP development keeps its separate development cookie name, and runtime metadata keeps prebuilt appcode independent of deployment mode.
regression_tests: pytincture/frontend/tests/lifecycle.test.mjs: CSRF cookie selection uses one explicit runtime mode

findings.disposition: Every generated asynchronous BFF and replay-state fetch carries an AbortController signal and aborts on timeout, cancellation, error, or completion. Streaming readers are cancelled in a bounded finally path.
findings.compatibility_note: Sync, async, streaming, moving chunks, and yield APIs remain; the browser releases abandoned network work sooner.

findings.disposition: Canonicalize service-worker cache keys to the expected asset version identity and bound/prune cache entries.
findings.compatibility_note: Unknown cache-busting query parameters no longer create distinct stored copies; the supported instance UUID/version key remains.

findings.disposition: Validate warm appcode entries from bounded relevant fingerprints instead of unbounded module-root traversal.
findings.compatibility_note: Relevant same-name development changes still invalidate the cache; production prebuilds avoid dynamic scans.

findings.disposition: Let replay-token waiters trigger another bounded refill rather than indexing beyond one batch.
findings.compatibility_note: Concurrency is preserved; accepted callers receive tokens without IndexError.

findings.disposition: Release isolated-process admission on every setup failure and double default capacity to eight per worker and four per stable user.
findings.compatibility_note: Optional isolated execution gains capacity; synchronous/async trusted mode and stateless load balancing are unchanged.
